skills.trigger: When evaluating complete opacification (white-out) of a hemithorax on a chest X-ray to determine the underlying etiology.
steps: Assess the position of the trachea and mediastinal structures relative to the opacified side.
If the trachea and mediastinum are shifted toward the unaffected (contralateral) side, identify the cause as a space-occupying lesion pushing structures away (e.g., massive pleural effusion).
If the trachea and mediastinum are shifted toward the affected (ipsilateral) side, identify the cause as volume loss pulling structures inward (e.g., total lung atelectasis or pneumonectomy).
If the trachea and mediastinum remain central, consider causes without significant mass effect or volume loss (e.g., pneumonia).
